name: Asia
blurb: From the cedar hills of Kyoto to the limestone bays of Vietnam, Asia rewards travellers who slow down and stay a while.
intro: Asia is the widest single canvas in travel: a continent where a two-hour flight moves you between a snow country, a monsoon coast and a megacity. We index it by intent — food, mountains, craft, coastline — rather than by country checklists.

name: Europe
blurb: Short distances, deep history and some of the most walkable cities and dramatic mountain valleys anywhere.
intro: Europe is the easiest continent to travel slowly. Rail networks make multi-country journeys practical, and the difference between a good trip and a great one is usually the choice of base town rather than the number of countries.

name: Middle East
blurb: Desert geology, layered history and a hospitality culture that changes how you think about being a guest.
intro: The Middle East has quietly become one of the most interesting regions for design-led stays and landscape travel — sandstone canyons, desert camps and cities investing heavily in culture.

name: Africa
blurb: Wildlife on a scale that resets your sense of proportion, alongside some of the world's great craft cities.
intro: Africa spans 54 countries and no single itinerary style. We cover it as two distinct travel modes: the wildlife journey, which is logistics-heavy and season-driven, and the city-and-craft journey, which rewards independent travel.

name: North America
blurb: Road-trip country: national parks, mountain towns and food cities with real depth.
intro: North America is best travelled by car and by region rather than by country. The distances are the story — plan fewer places and longer stays.

name: South America
blurb: Andean altitude, Patagonian wind and some of the last genuinely wild trekking on earth.
intro: South America asks more of travellers than most regions — altitude, distance, weather — and returns more. Build in buffer days; the continent does not reward tight scheduling.

name: Oceania
blurb: Compact, dramatic and outdoors-first — fiords, alpine lakes and long empty coastlines.
intro: Oceania is the region where landscape density is highest per kilometre driven. New Zealand in particular packs a continent's worth of terrain into a week's drive.

name: India
blurb: A subcontinent of distinct travel countries — Himalayan, coastal, desert, southern — each deserving its own trip.
intro: India is treated here as its own region rather than one country in Asia, because it travels like a continent. The mistake most first trips make is covering too much ground; the fix is choosing one of its four travel geographies and staying in it.
